hints: Calculate the initial and final kinetic energies: $E_{k,i} = \frac{1}{2}(75)(10^2)$ and $E_{k,f} = \frac{1}{2}(75)(5^2)$.
Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained: $\Delta E_p = mgh = 75(10)(700\sin 1.5^\circ)$.
Write the work-energy balance equation: $W_F + E_{k,i} = E_{k,f} + \Delta E_p + W_{\text{res}}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the kinetic energies at the bottom and top of the hill:
$$E_{k,\text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2}(75)(10^2) = 0.5(75)(100) = 3750\text{ J}$$
$$E_{k,\text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}(75)(5^2) = 0.5(75)(25) = 937.5\text{ J}$$

Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy, where vertical height $h = 700\sin 1.5^\circ$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 75(10)(700\sin 1.5^\circ) = 525000\sin 1.5^\circ \approx 13742.9\text{ J}$$

Express the work done by the driving force $F$ over the $700\text{ m}$ distance as $W_F = 700F$ and apply the work-energy theorem:
$$W_F + E_{k,\text{initial}} = E_{k,\text{final}} + \Delta E_p + W_{\text{res}}$$
$$700F + 3750 = 937.5 + 13742.9 + 2000 = 16680.4$$
$$700F = 16680.4 - 3750 = 12930.4$$

Solve for the force $F$:
$$F = \frac{12930.4}{700} \approx 18.472\text{ N} \approx 18.5\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy principle in the form that balances energy input with mechanical energy changes and work done against resistance:
$$W_{\text{driving}} + E_{k,\text{initial}} = E_{k,\text{final}} + \Delta E_p + W_{\text{res}}$$

Calculate each energy term separately with $m = 75\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
- Initial kinetic energy at $u = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,\text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2} \times 75 \times 10^2 = 37.5 \times 100 = 3750\text{ J}$$
- Final kinetic energy at $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,\text{final}} = \frac{1}{2} \times 75 \times 5^2 = 37.5 \times 25 = 937.5\text{ J}$$
- Gravitational potential energy gained on the incline ($d = 700\text{ m}$, $\alpha = 1.5^\circ$):
$$h = 700\sin 1.5^\circ$$
$$\Delta E_p = 75 \times 10 \times 700\sin 1.5^\circ = 525000\sin 1.5^\circ$$
$$\sin 1.5^\circ \approx 0.02617695$$
$$\Delta E_p = 525000 \times 0.02617695 \approx 13742.90\text{ J}$$
- Work done against resistance: $W_{\text{res}} = 2000\text{ J}$.

Express the work done by the cyclist's forward force $F$:
$$W_{\text{driving}} = F \times d = 700F$$

Assemble the full equation:
$$700F + 3750 = 937.5 + 13742.90 + 2000$$
Sum the right-hand side:
$$937.5 + 13742.90 + 2000 = 16680.40\text{ J}$$
Subtract $3750$ from both sides:
$$700F = 16680.40 - 3750 = 12930.40$$
Divide by $700$:
$$F = \frac{12930.40}{700} \approx 18.472\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $F = 18.5\text{ N}$.
